## Executive Summary

1. **What the prize is.** The Earth Optimization Prize is the institutional shell for an open-source coordination game: help humanity raise global median income and healthy life years within {{< var prize_pool_resolution_years_nounit >}} years.
2. **What success means.** At year {{< var prize_pool_resolution_years_nounit >}}, success means global HALE (healthy life expectancy) reaches {{< var wishonia_projected_hale_year_15 >}} and global median income reaches {{< var wishonia_trajectory_avg_income_year_15 >}} (modeled ceiling, not forecast; see [GDP Trajectories](../economics/gdp-trajectories.qmd) [@gdp-trajectories-paper-2025] for the compounding model).
3. **How PRIZE works.** Depositors fund one pool until year {{< var prize_pool_resolution_years_nounit >}}. Targets missed: depositors divide the realized pool pro rata.
4. **How VOTE works.** Recruit one verified referendum participant, earn one point. On success, the pool routes to VOTE point-holders.
5. **What institutions are being asked to do.** Three tiers: activation ({{< var global_coordination_activation_budget >}}), visible pool seed ({{< var prize_pool_retirement_equivalent_principal >}}), and eventual ceiling ({{< var prize_pool_potential_max_size >}}). The first ask is {{< var global_coordination_activation_budget >}} to underwrite recruitment, verification, and the first public Scoreboard.
6. **Why it matters.** Status quo is not stable. Governance dysfunction already costs {{< var political_dysfunction_tax_per_person_annual >}} per person per year in suppressed growth and misallocated resources ([Political Dysfunction Tax](../appendix/political-dysfunction-tax.qmd) [@political-dysfunction-tax-paper-2025]). The [destructive economy](../economics/gdp-trajectories.qmd) [@gdp-trajectories-paper-2025] reaches the 50% Terminal Parasitic Load Threshold (the point where half the economy is destructive and stealing beats creating) in {{< var destructive_economy_years_to_50pct_gdp >}} if current trends continue.

## The Problem Statement

- Your governments are a [misaligned superintelligence](../economics/central-banks.qmd) whose stated objective function is to make you [2% poorer each year](../economics/central-banks.qmd#goal-2-stable-prices-take-2-per-year) and keep you [too busy working to notice](../economics/central-banks.qmd#goal-1-maximum-employment-keep-everyone-busy). Since 1913, they have [printed so much money](../economics/central-banks.qmd) that they've devalued your paycheck by 96%, in order to spend {{< var cumulative_military_spending_fed_era >}} killing {{< var money_printer_war_deaths_nounit >}} people in unpopular wars without asking your permission to have them [@sipri-milex-2024; @crs-war-costs-2010]. The global annual murder budget is {{< var global_military_spending_annual_2024 >}}, which is {{< var military_to_government_clinical_trials_spending_ratio >}} times what governments spend [testing which medicines work](../appendix/global-government-medical-research-spending.qmd).
- The [destructive economy](../economics/gdp-trajectories.qmd) [@gdp-trajectories-paper-2025] is already {{< var global_destructive_economy_pct_gdp >}} of GDP, reaches 25% in {{< var destructive_economy_years_to_25pct_gdp >}}, and hits the 50% Terminal Parasitic Load Threshold in {{< var destructive_economy_years_to_50pct_gdp >}}, where whatever gets created gets looted.
- The year-15 status quo path is global median income of {{< var current_trajectory_avg_income_year_15 >}}. The modeled optimal-governance target is {{< var wishonia_trajectory_avg_income_year_15 >}}, with GDP at roughly {{< var wishonia_trajectory_gdp_vs_current_trajectory_multiplier_year_15 >}} the status quo trajectory. The gap is that large because the destructive economy compounds: on the status quo path it keeps moving toward the point where half the economy is destructive and new value gets looted as fast as it is created, dragging median income down while the optimal path redirects that waste into productive compounding through three specific channels: disease-burden recovery (preventable disease and conflict currently consume {{< var global_destructive_economy_pct_gdp >}} of GDP), military-to-R&D reallocation, and R&D spillover multipliers (see [Political Dysfunction Tax](../appendix/political-dysfunction-tax.qmd) [@political-dysfunction-tax-paper-2025] for the full waste ledger and compounding derivation). The difference is not optimism vs. realism; it is compounding waste vs. compounding investment over 15 years.
- What that 1% buys: the [1% Treaty](../solution/1-percent-treaty.qmd) redirects {{< var treaty_annual_funding >}}/year from military budgets to pragmatic clinical trials. That single reallocation expands trial capacity {{< var dfda_trial_capacity_multiplier >}}, accelerates the drug-disease search space from {{< var status_quo_queue_clearance_years >}} to {{< var dfda_queue_clearance_years >}}, and averts {{< var dfda_trial_capacity_plus_efficacy_lag_lives_saved_nounit >}} deaths at {{< var treaty_cost_per_daly_trial_capacity_plus_efficacy_lag >}} per DALY ({{< var treaty_vs_bed_nets_multiplier >}} more cost-effective than anti-malaria bed nets) [@1-pct-treaty-impact-paper-2025].
- The minimum serious first test is that treaty: are humans willing to redirect even 1% from weapons to medicine?

## How It Works (The 90-Second Version)

**PRIZE deposits** fund the same pool that compounds through the [wishocratic fund](../economics/wishocratic-investment-fund.qmd). The pooled vehicle is, by definition, an accredited investor, so a $1 depositor gets access to the same venture and private equity asset class ({{< var venture_gross_return >}} gross returns) that conventional retirement accounts are legally locked out of. Because the pool diversifies across the entire VC/PE sector rather than concentrating in a handful of funds, individual-fund risk is erased. Crowd allocation ({{< var crowd_decision_accuracy >}} accuracy vs. {{< var expert_decision_accuracy >}} for expert fund managers [@surowiecki-2004]) replaces fee-charging committees, and global diversification eliminates home-country bias. The structural result is {{< var prize_pool_annual_return >}} annually, nearly triple conventional retirement at {{< var conventional_retirement_return >}} (see [Wishocratic Investment Fund](../economics/wishocratic-investment-fund.qmd) for the full derivation). That same capital stops propping up rent-seeking oligopolies surviving on regulatory moats and starts funding the most innovative new companies across every sector. PRIZE deposits are locked capital, not a redeem-anytime savings account. It stays with the depositor's verified account or legal-entity account until resolution, subject to recovery and lawful successor control. If the targets are missed, depositors divide the realized pool pro rata. If the targets are met, the pool goes to VOTE point-holders, not depositors. See the [prize protocol](../appendix/earth-optimization-prize-protocol.qmd) [@earth-optimization-prize-protocol-paper-2025] for the full specification.

**VOTE points** are the public-facing game score. Recruit one verified referendum participant into the first [1% Treaty](../solution/1-percent-treaty.qmd) [@1-pct-treaty-impact-paper-2025] vote, earn one point. VOTE points stay with the verified account that earned them and are not publicly tradable inside the protocol, so coalition credit stays with recruiters rather than speculators. Registration asks two questions: (1) yes or no on the 1% Treaty, the smallest serious test of whether humans are willing to redirect even 1% from weapons to medicine, and (2) how much military vs. clinical trials, with [Optimitron](../solution/optimocracy.qmd) (the evidence engine that scores policy options by measured outcomes) [@optimocracy-paper-2025] evidence. The basic flow is designed to fit on a phone in under a minute.

| Year-15 objective | Current baseline | Year-15 target |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **Global HALE** | {{< var global_hale_current >}} | {{< var wishonia_projected_hale_year_15 >}} |
| **Global median income** | {{< var current_trajectory_avg_income_year_15 >}} (status quo at year 15) | {{< var wishonia_trajectory_avg_income_year_15 >}} (modeled ceiling; see [GDP Trajectories](../economics/gdp-trajectories.qmd)) |

The public signal is the **Earth Optimization Scoreboard**, updated in real time: global median HALE, global median income, number of votes, percent support for the 1% Treaty, current wishocratic allocation between military and clinical trials, and size of the Earth Optimization Prize Pool. Polls are ignorable. Petitions are ignorable. A large verified Scoreboard is harder to dismiss.

## Contributor Outcomes

Let `D` be your deposit. The pool compounds through the wishocratic fund regardless of whether the year-15 targets are met (the fund invests productively either way). The only question is who receives the realized pool at resolution.

| Scenario | What happens to your deposit | What happens to your VOTE points | World-side outcome |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| **Status quo retirement** | Conventional market: `D × {{< var conventional_retirement_15yr_multiple >}}` | N/A | Current trajectory continues. |
| **PRIZE fails** | Depositors divide realized pool: `D × {{< var prize_pool_15yr_multiple >}}` | VOTE points expire worthless. | Status quo branch. |
| **Objectives met** | Deposit routes to VOTE point-holders, not back to you. | Each point pays {{< var vote_token_potential_value >}}. | +{{< var treaty_trajectory_lifetime_income_gain_per_capita >}} to +{{< var wishonia_trajectory_lifetime_income_gain_per_capita >}} cumulative lifetime income (compounded over ~48 remaining years) for everyone. |

**Worked example: $100 deposit + 2 VOTE points.**

- *Targets missed:* You get back `$100 × {{< var prize_pool_15yr_multiple >}}` = $1,110 from the pool. Your VOTE points pay nothing. You still beat a conventional retirement account (`$100 × {{< var conventional_retirement_15yr_multiple >}}` = $257).
- *Targets met:* Your $100 deposit goes to VOTE point-holders. Your 2 VOTE points pay `2 × {{< var vote_token_potential_value >}} = {{< var vote_2_claims_payout >}}`. Plus the world-side gain: {{< var treaty_personal_upside_blend >}} to {{< var wishonia_personal_upside_blend >}} in modeled personal upside from higher income and longer healthy life.

Two VOTE points are meaningful upside for small contributors, but not a sufficient standalone case for large depositors or institutions. Large institutions should be pitched on activation, public-good upside, and coalition formation, not on a retail-style “deposit plus 2 points” story.

## Why the Mechanism Exists

Your species has never built a system that measures the two things everyone agrees on (healthy life years and income), publishes the score, and pays whoever moves it. You argue about drug policy without tracking whether fewer people die. You argue about military spending without tracking whether it makes you safer. You argue about healthcare without tracking whether anyone gets healthier. The prize does not resolve these arguments. It makes them irrelevant. Two numbers. Did they move? Pay whoever moved them.

That missing Scoreboard is underneath five specific problems the prize is trying to solve at once:

1. **Awareness.** Most people do not know how large the upside of better governance and cheaper clinical trials is.
2. **Pluralistic ignorance.** People assume nobody else would support large reform until they can see the Scoreboard proving otherwise.
3. **Coordination.** The public has diffuse interests and no standard mechanism for committing capital together.
4. **Solution search.** Nobody agrees in advance which package is best, so the prize pays for outcomes and lets better packages compete.
5. **On-ramp.** Complex reform bundles need a simple first action; `deposit, register, recruit` is that action.

### 1. Nobody Knows Solutions Exist

Most humans have never heard that pragmatic clinical trials (streamlined trials run inside routine care) cost {{< var dfda_pragmatic_trial_cost_per_patient >}} per patient (vs. {{< var traditional_phase3_cost_per_patient >}} traditional) [@dfda-impact-paper-2025]. That redirecting 1% of military spending to medical research yields a societal ROI of {{< var treaty_roi_existing_drugs_only >}} (QALY-valued lives saved per dollar of campaign cost) [@1-pct-treaty-impact-paper-2025]. That {{< var existing_drugs_efficacy_lag_deaths_total_nounit >}} people have already died (since 1962) waiting for drugs that were proven to work but stuck in regulatory queues [@invisible-graveyard-paper-2025]. That the total cost of buying passage of any policy through legal democratic channels in the United States is {{< var treaty_campaign_total_cost >}}, with ROI exceeding {{< var treaty_roi_existing_drugs_only >}} [@cost-of-change-paper-2025].

VOTE points make millions of people willing to have a conversation they would otherwise avoid. Each recruitment forces the recruit through evidence (cost per life saved for military spending vs. clinical trials, the efficacy lag death toll, the economic returns). The registration process is the education. The recruitment reward is what makes the education propagate.

### 2. Everyone Who Knows Assumes They Are Alone

Your economists call it pluralistic ignorance. Nearly every human would prefer a world without war and treatable disease, and an extra {{< var treaty_trajectory_lifetime_income_gain_per_capita >}} in cumulative lifetime income (compounded over ~48 remaining years) [@gdp-trajectories-paper-2025]. If every human realized that nearly every other human wants the same thing, it would be done tomorrow and the world would be unrecognizable. Instead, everyone assumes massive reform is crazy because they assume nobody else would agree to it. This is the dumbest reason a civilization has ever continued dying.

Every verified registration is a publicly verifiable signal. The Scoreboard aggregates across all participating pools in real time. As the number climbs from thousands to millions to hundreds of millions, the belief that "nobody would ever agree to this" becomes empirically falsifiable. You can see that they already did. The [referendum](global-referendum.qmd) does not create demand for not dying. The demand is there. The Scoreboard makes it impossible to pretend it is not.

### 3. The Public Cannot Coordinate Against Concentrated Interests

One of your economists noticed this in 1965 and named it "the logic of collective action" [-@olson1965]. Concentrated interests (defense contractors, pharmaceutical monopolies) face high per-capita stakes and coordinate easily. The general public has tiny individual stakes in any single policy fight and cannot mount a proportional response, even though they are the ones dying of untreated diseases, bearing regulatory delay, and subsidizing military spending that returns {{< var economic_multiplier_military_spending >}} per dollar [@military-spending-economic-multiplier].

Your species identified the exact mechanism by which your governance fails, published it, assigned it in universities, and then continued to be governed by it for sixty years.

But Olson's problem is downstream of awareness and pluralistic ignorance. The public has the money (global household wealth: {{< var global_household_wealth_usd >}}, vs. {{< var concentrated_interest_sector_market_cap_usd >}} held by concentrated opposition sectors [@iab-paper-2025]). It does not have the coordination mechanism. Once the recruitment incentive has solved the awareness problem and the Scoreboard has shattered pluralistic ignorance, PRIZE deposits provide that mechanism: a growing, visible pool of committed capital. No central organizer. No charity. No altruism required. Just millions of people acting in financial self-interest, pointed at the same two numbers.

### 4. Nobody Knows Which Solutions to Implement

The prize does not prescribe a solution. It pays for outcomes: median healthy life years and median real after-tax income. Anyone, anywhere, using any legal method, who causes either number to rise gets paid proportionally. This is an Earth Optimization Game. Institutionally, it is a prize-and-pool mechanism. The [current Earth Optimization manual](https://manual.warondisease.org) is the current open-source instruction manual, not the goal and not a sacred blueprint. It exists because humans need a starting manual for how to play. The prize exists to fund whichever implementation manual works better in practice. There are {{< var global_population_2024_nounit >}} of you and AIs that are almost certainly smarter than its authors. If a better design exists, the prize will find it.

This makes the search decentralized. No committee decides which reforms to fund. Millions of financially motivated participants search for, advocate, and implement whatever moves the two numbers. A researcher who discovers a cheaper trial design profits. A lobbyist who passes legislation profits. A nonprofit that recruits a million referendum voters profits. The mechanism is agnostic about how. It engineers the incentives so that the collective intelligence of your entire species is pointed at two measurements instead of scattered across a thousand arguments about which measurement matters.

Your species has tried the obvious alternatives. Advance Market Commitments [@kremer2020] say "we will buy the thing if you build it," which works when the thing is a vaccine but not when the thing is systemic reform. Challenge prizes give a fixed payout to the first team across the finish line, then stop paying. Direct government procurement funds whatever the procurer thinks will work, which is the current system, and it is producing capture. Prediction markets tell you what will win but do not cause implementation. Capital-weighted governance systems suffer the same capture problem: the actors with the deepest pockets set the agenda. A prize with published scoring, adversarial challenges, and automatic replacement is the one structure where capturing it requires beating every challenger on verified metrics simultaneously. That is not capture-proof. But it is capture-expensive.

### 5. Complex Reforms Have No On-Ramp

The [1% Treaty](../solution/1-percent-treaty.qmd) [@1-pct-treaty-impact-paper-2025], FDA reform, wishocratic allocation, cross-jurisdictional policy optimization: each is a hard sell individually. Each requires explaining an elaborate mechanism to people who have been trained to assume nothing works. The prize is the simple entry point. Deposit $1, keep a failure-branch claim on the same pool if nothing works, and help route it to VOTE point-holders if the world actually improves. One sentence. One decision. The $1 minimum is the on-ramp, not a claim that every participant must become a large 15-year capital provider.

Once someone makes a PRIZE deposit or earns a VOTE claim, they discover the component reforms through the recruitment and registration process. The treaty. The trial cost data. The allocation evidence. The prize is the funnel into everything else. It converts "this sounds too complicated" into "I put in $1 and either diseases get cured or I still have a claim on the pool, so why not." The complex reforms ride behind the simple instrument.

## The Exponential Math

On Wishonia, if one person tells two people and each of them tells two people, the math handles the rest. The point is not that everyone becomes a recruiter. The point is that small repeated actions can compound into politically legible scale much faster than most readers intuit.

| Round | Cumulative people | What that looks like |
|:---|:---|:---|
| 0 | 1 | You |
| 10 | 1,024 | A large lecture hall |
| 15 | 32,768 | A small town |
| 20 | 1,048,576 | A city |
| 25 | 33,554,432 | A country |
| 28 | 268,435,456 | Hundreds of millions; globally visible |
| 32 | 4,294,967,296 | Roughly the modeled global coordination target |
| 33 | 8,589,934,592 | Everyone on Earth |

32 rounds. Not 32 years. 32 rounds. If each round takes a week, that is eight months. If each round takes a month, that is two years and eight months. The important point is not the payout headline. It is that the Scoreboard can move from one person to politically legible world scale on ordinary human timescales rather than civilizational ones. Real referral chains have attrition; not every round doubles perfectly. The table shows the mathematical ceiling. Even with heavy dropout, the distance from one person to politically legible scale is measured in dozens of rounds, not decades.

The modeled end-state coordination target is {{< var global_coordination_target_supporters_nounit >}} people, or {{< var global_coordination_target_pct >}} of humanity. That is the canonical public headcount target for the prize. VOTE points make coalition-building worth doing. The Scoreboard makes that coalition legible. At scale, treaty passage is expected well before the pool matures.

For institutions, the first decision is not whether to move a massive share of global capital immediately. It is whether to underwrite three distinct jobs: make mass participation credible, seed the PRIZE pool enough that long-dated upside feels real, and then scale the capital base once the network is legible. A foundation consortium is the expected first mover. One extraordinary institution could still do the whole thing.

"Do nothing" is not a neutral baseline. It is a bet that the trends in the Problem Statement reverse without intervention.

## This Is a Favorable Bet, Not a Donation

**PRIZE deposits** are the conditional commitment. Your money stays with depositors on failure and routes to VOTE point-holders on success.

| | If the plan succeeds | If the plan fails |
|---|---|---|
| **A PRIZE deposit** | Pool distributes to VOTE point-holders who built the coalition. Your lifetime income rose by {{< var treaty_trajectory_lifetime_income_gain_per_capita >}} like everyone else's. | Depositors divide the realized pool pro rata at year {{< var prize_pool_resolution_years_nounit >}}. |
| **The world** | Diseases get cured, incomes rise, destructive economy stops compounding | Terminal Parasitic Load Threshold in {{< var destructive_economy_years_to_50pct_gdp >}}; destructive economy already {{< var global_destructive_economy_pct_gdp >}} of GDP and accelerating |

Mechanisms that keep the same pool intact on failure while only routing it to VOTE point-holders on verified success are unusually favorable compared with ordinary political donations.

At the current modeled pool growth rate, the same pool compounds at {{< var prize_pool_annual_return >}} annually, reaching {{< var prize_pool_15yr_multiple >}} over {{< var prize_pool_resolution_years_nounit >}} years before branch routing. That is a modeling reference, not a guaranteed depositor payout.
:::

The break-even probability shift for any given contribution is small because the per-capita stakes are large:

| Your unreimbursed contribution | Break-even probability shift (Treaty floor) | Break-even probability shift (Wishonia) |
|---|---|---|
| `$1K` | `0.0067%` | `0.0019%` |
| `$10K` | `0.067%` | `0.019%` |
| `$100K` | `0.671%` | `0.192%` |
| `$1M` | `6.71%` | `1.92%` |

But does a $1K contribution actually shift probability by 0.0067%? You do not need to be the marginal dollar that tips the scale. You need to believe that more campaign capital makes success more likely than less, which is nearly tautological for political adoption. Those thresholds also treat PRIZE deposits like unreimbursed spending, so they are biased against contributing. They survive heavy skepticism: if you think the per-capita gain is 100x smaller than modeled, the break-even for $1K is still only 0.67%. The math does not require trusting the model. It requires believing the model is not off by more than four orders of magnitude. And the ceiling cost of achieving the policy change is already bounded: {{< var treaty_campaign_total_cost >}} for the United States, {{< var global_political_reform_investment >}} globally, with societal ROI exceeding {{< var treaty_roi_existing_drugs_only >}} for military-to-health reallocation [@cost-of-change-paper-2025].

Outcome-contingent funding and threshold-triggered coordination are standard mechanism-design tools [@tabarrok1998]. The Chenoweth threshold ({{< var global_population_activism_threshold_pct >}}) is best understood here as a historical lower bound for when movements become hard to ignore, not as the prize's canonical end-state coordination target. The RECOVERY trial was run by Oxford and published in the New England Journal of Medicine. Every building block is peer-reviewed. The combination is new.

**The free-rider problem has a structural answer.** If success benefits everyone, why not wait and let others pay? Because non-contributors do not earn VOTE points. They get the population-wide income gain (everyone does), but they miss the VOTE payout that recruiters earn. Free-riding means giving up the recruitment reward to save the smallest possible entry ticket. Early contributors raise the probability of success, which raises the expected value for later contributors, creating a coordination game that runs on arithmetic rather than altruism.

Delay is not neutral. Each person can only be recruited once, and every month spent waiting gives the status quo more time to compound while the Scoreboard stays smaller than it could be.

The selfish case for the prize is bigger than either instrument. It is the size of the future they are trying to buy.

## What To Do Right Now

1. **Deposit $1.** PRIZE deposit. One pool, one resolution date, pro-rata failure claim.
2. **Answer 2 questions.** 30 seconds. Treaty yes/no, allocation slider with evidence.
3. **Recruit 2 people.** Get two more verified participants onto the Scoreboard.

### If You Have Reach, Do the Bigger Version Now

- **Funders:** pick one lane this week and publish the commitment so other participants can coordinate around it.
- **Researchers / builders:** publish one fork, attack, or replacement component this week rather than waiting for perfect certainty.
- **Host institutions:** announce a 90-day pilot, publish the rules, convene the panel, fund the first adversarial-review pool, and launch the Scoreboard.
- **Media:** publish one briefing or story that treats the Scoreboard and futures table as live public infrastructure, not a curiosity.

The first milestones: initiating host announced, rules published, expert panel formed, first bounty pool funded, first Scoreboard live, first credible submissions received. Then 1,024 verified participants, then 32,768, then a visibly serious pool. Once the mechanism clears those milestones, the question stops being "is this real?" and becomes "how fast is it compounding?"

That is the ordinary-participant ask: three actions, under two minutes. If the prize fails, your deposit still has a pro-rata claim on the realized pool. If the prize succeeds, your PRIZE deposit helped push the world onto a far better branch. The mechanism is open, the Scoreboard is public, and the first step is deliberately small. Whether it matters depends on how quickly enough people decide the arithmetic is worth acting on.

## How It Starts

The instruments deploy in order, and each stage builds the audience for the next. A credible institution can be the initiating node for this process. That role is to host, convene, seed, and publish, not to become the sovereign of the mechanism. The rules, interfaces, and measurement layers should remain open and replaceable so launch does not create a single point of failure.

**Stage 1: The [Planetary Constitutional Convention](planetary-constitutional-convention.qmd) [@planetary-constitutional-convention-paper-2025] (weeks to months).** A credible host institution can initiate the network by publishing the rules, convening the expert panel, funding adversarial review, and launching the first public scoreboard. It does not need to endorse the current manual as final truth. It hosts the convention that improves it. Teams fork the [current Earth Optimization manual](https://manual.warondisease.org), improve it, and replace the wrong parts. Expert panel filters for constitutional compliance. Adversarial review catches what the panel misses. [Wishocracy](../solution/wishocracy.qmd) [@wishocracy-paper-2025] ranks the survivors. The ratified version becomes the current manual. PRIZE deposits can begin during this stage, because the prize pool funds itself regardless of which revision is ratified.

**Stage 2: PRIZE deposits and the referendum (weeks to months).** PRIZE deposits are the simplest on-ramp. Every depositor learns what the prize is for. The PRIZE deposit is the simplest public coordination signal. Meanwhile, the [referendum platform](global-referendum.qmd) launches: voters set their preferred military-to-health allocation via [wishocratic sliders](../solution/wishocracy.qmd), and every recruiter who brings a verified participant earns VOTE points. The referendum grows because recruitment is rewarded.

**Stage 3: Scoreboard and momentum (months).** The Scoreboard climbs in public: votes, treaty support, allocation results, prize pool size, and the two outcome metrics that give the whole thing its point. Each new cohort of participants makes the next cohort easier to convince. Politicians notice.

**Stage 4: The lobbying campaign (months to years).** By now, millions of voters have registered preferences, the PRIZE pool is large enough to be taken seriously, and the Scoreboard shows that the coalition is real. The [current Earth Optimization manual](earth-optimization-protocol-v1.qmd) [@earth-optimization-protocol-2025] describes how implementation financing converts the Scoreboard into political pressure.

**Stage 5+: Implementation.** Once one binding path succeeds, budget authority starts shifting real resources. Implementers compete inside the current ratified instruction manual to supply the cheapest verified pieces, and later revisions can still replace the whole manual if they genuinely dominate it.

The funnel is: the Planetary Constitutional Convention stress-tests the manual. PRIZE deposits create awareness. Awareness creates referendum voters. Voters earn VOTE points. VOTE points create an aligned recruiter base. The coalition provides the political pressure and financing base to pass the treaty. Each stage builds the coordination infrastructure for the next one. Nobody has to coordinate this centrally. The incentives coordinate it.

## How the Prize Moves Money {#how-money-moves-full-mechanism}

Everything the prize exists to produce is either healthy life years or income. Paying separately for budget reallocation or trial enrollment is paying for plumbing that may or may not deliver water. Pay for water.

**The PRIZE pool trigger.** At year {{< var prize_pool_resolution_years_nounit >}}: targets met, the pool distributes to VOTE point-holders; targets missed, depositors divide it pro rata.

**Why better ideas win, not extract.** If a superior revision appears, VOTE point-holders shift recruitment toward it because doing so maximizes their own payout. The biggest reward is outcome perpetuity: a continuing share that only flows while results keep being produced. The protocol itself is replaceable: a strictly better selection mechanism replaces the current one under the same replacement rule. The two numbers do not change. Everything building toward them is improvable plumbing.

## The Numbers (Institutional Detail)

**What is the first institutional number?** The canonical activation threshold is the capital required to make {{< var global_coordination_target_pct >}} participation credible through direct referral incentives, verification, payment rails, and global launch operations:

{{< var global_coordination_activation_budget_latex >}}

The planning midpoint is {{< var global_coordination_activation_budget >}}. That comes from a research-backed blended reward of {{< var global_coordination_activation_reward_per_verified_participant >}} per successful verified participant, plus {{< var global_coordination_verification_and_payment_cost_per_participant >}} in variable verification and payment operations, plus {{< var global_coordination_platform_and_operations_cost >}} in fixed platform and launch costs. This is the main institutional ask.

**What visible PRIZE seed makes the upside feel large?** A separate benchmark asks how much pool capital would make two VOTE points look retirement-equivalent on success for a representative saver:

{{< var prize_pool_retirement_equivalent_principal_latex >}}

That stronger-incentive benchmark is {{< var prize_pool_retirement_equivalent_principal >}}. It is a visible-pool benchmark, not the minimum capital required to make humanity participate.

**How large can the prize pool get later?** The canonical capital ceiling is the global retirement asset base: {{< var global_retirement_assets >}}. If that capital compounds through the wishocratic fund at {{< var prize_pool_annual_return >}} (modeled structural return, not guaranteed) over {{< var prize_pool_resolution_years_nounit >}} years:

{{< var prize_pool_potential_max_size_latex >}}

The potential max pool is {{< var prize_pool_potential_max_size >}}. That is the scale vision: what happens if large retirement and institutional capital eventually joins a network that is already politically and operationally real. It is the end-state ceiling, not the opening board ask.

**What headcount does the payout headline assume?** The payout headline is secondary to the activation threshold. It answers a narrower question: what long-dated VOTE upside could one point represent if the network reaches the canonical coordination target and the pool later scales?

The referendum is designed to solve the usual turnout problem:

| Dimension | Your elections | This referendum |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **Effort** | Hours in line, research candidates | 30 seconds on a phone |
| **Financial reward** | $0 | {{< var vote_token_potential_value >}} modeled success payout |
| **Pivotality** | ~1 in 30 million in a typical US national election [@gelman2012] | Direct payout proportional to contribution |
| **Outcome fidelity** | Politician may ignore you after winning | Funds flow to verified implementation |

Your species turns out at 50-65% for elections despite getting paid nothing. This referendum adds a contingent payout, direct attribution, and a public Scoreboard. The canonical payout headline assumes the modeled global coordination target of {{< var global_coordination_target_pct >}}:

{{< var global_coordination_target_supporters_latex >}}

At that headcount, {{< var global_coordination_target_supporters_nounit >}} people participate and split the success-side pool by referred votes. One referred voter is the canonical point unit; "2 points" is the recruiter example. The canonical potential payout per VOTE point at the coordination target is:

{{< var vote_token_potential_value_latex >}}

So the institutional stack is: first make mass participation credible ({{< var global_coordination_activation_budget >}}), then make success-side upside visibly real ({{< var prize_pool_retirement_equivalent_principal >}}), then scale the network into a civilization-sized capital allocator ({{< var prize_pool_potential_max_size >}} ceiling).

**Why more pools make everyone richer.** The protocol does not need a single pool. It needs a single *metric standard*. Any pool that measures the same two terminal outcomes (median HALY, median income) and uses proof-of-personhood for deduplication automatically joins the reward network. A verified person claims proportionally from every participating pool, regardless of which one recorded their vote. Japan launches a pool, the EU launches a pool, the Gates Foundation launches a pool. The combined reward grows with each new entrant. A "competing" pool is actually a deposit. Spending money to "attack" the network is indistinguishable from donating to it. Think of email: you can run your own server; all servers interoperate; running your own extends the network rather than fragmenting it.

**What the protocol must solve.** Six capabilities: (1) identity layer (one person, one vote, cross-pool), (2) pool registry, (3) cross-pool claim settlement, (4) Scoreboard aggregation, (5) terminal metric oracle, (6) claim mechanics. The companion [protocol specification](../appendix/earth-optimization-prize-protocol.qmd) [@earth-optimization-protocol-2025] specifies how.

## Why Public Choice Theory Approves

Public choice theory says governments are run by humans who care about reelection, career advancement, and reputation. This is not a design flaw. It is a design constraint. The prize works with it, because no one has to become good:

- **Depositors** commit capital because they retain a failure-branch claim on the same pool and buy a better future on success.
- **Recruiters** recruit because every verified participant earns them a VOTE point.
- **Entrepreneurs** compete for a giant implementation franchise.
- **Politicians** notice a growing Scoreboard of verified voters who care about two numbers.
- **Researchers and auditors** compete for the authority to validate what works.
- **Citizens** get simpler choices and more visible returns from participation.

Every participant is doing exactly what they would do anyway, except pointed at diseases instead of each other.

## FAQ for Skeptics

| Objection | Answer |
|:---|:---|
| "This will never work" | The ceiling cost of passage is {{< var treaty_campaign_total_cost >}} for the US, {{< var global_political_reform_investment >}} globally. Societal ROI exceeds {{< var treaty_roi_existing_drugs_only >}} [@cost-of-change-paper-2025]. "Political impossibility" is a capital allocation problem, not a physics problem. |
| "Does this require trusting one institution?" | No. A credible host can initiate the network, but it should not be the root of trust. The rules, contracts, interfaces, and measurement layers should remain open, forkable, and replaceable so another host can continue the process if the first one fails. |
| "Does hosting mean endorsing the current manual?" | No. A host institution can endorse the convention, the metric standard, and the red-team process without declaring the current draft correct. Stage 1 exists to improve the manual if a better version exists. |
| "I'd lose my $1" | On failure, depositors divide the realized pool pro rata. On success, the deposit funds the pool by design. The selfish case is that the rest of your life got much larger than the dollar you put in. |
| "Can I sell my claim?" | Not inside the protocol. PRIZE stays with the depositor's verified account until resolution. VOTE stays with the verified recruiter who earned it. Private contracts can exist outside the protocol, like assigning future royalties, but the protocol does not broker or enforce them. |
| "Why can't PRIZE be withdrawn early?" | Because a redeem-anytime exit right would let depositors drain the pool as success became more likely. The prize only works if the capital remains committed until the measurement date. |
| "What if I die or lose access?" | Claims belong to a verified account, not a fragile device. The system needs account recovery, beneficiary designation, and lawful successor control so a 15-year claim does not disappear because you lost your phone or your heirs need to prove who they are. |
| "Nobody else will participate" | That IS the problem the prize exists to solve. Your deposit is the proof that someone does. The Scoreboard makes everyone else's participation visible. |
| "I don't understand the mechanism" | You do not need to. Deposit $1, answer 2 questions, recruit 2 people. |
| "Why can't VOTE points be traded?" | Tradability would buy liquidity but invert the signal: outsiders could buy coalition credit without doing coalition work. The public signal this design relies on is simpler: verified participant count, referendum growth, and a visible pool of committed capital. |
| "Won't someone game the metrics?" | Mortality is binary and hard to fake across millions of people. Median income requires improving the middle of the distribution, not just the top. And the adversarial challenge window means anyone who catches gaming can post a bond, present evidence, and claw back the payout. |

## What the Current Manual Covers (and Where It Needs Improvement)

The full table of what the [current Earth Optimization manual](https://manual.warondisease.org) covers, paper by paper, and the minimum functions any serious implementation manual still has to solve, is in the [Planetary Constitutional Convention](planetary-constitutional-convention.qmd) [@planetary-constitutional-convention-paper-2025]. The prize asks one question: *which implementation manual can actually cause the verified improvements?* We wrote the current manual as a starting instruction manual, not a sacred blueprint. If any part of it is wrong, improve the manual or replace that part with something better. We expect that to happen.

## Help Improve the Manual

If you think the [current Earth Optimization manual](https://manual.warondisease.org) is wrong or incomplete, fork it and improve it through the [Planetary Constitutional Convention](planetary-constitutional-convention.qmd) [@planetary-constitutional-convention-paper-2025]. The point is not to submit a rival artifact. The point is to help humanity win faster.

## Why This Works or Gets Replaced

There are only two stable outcomes:

1. **The current instruction manual is mostly right but incomplete.** Then whoever augments it with the missing functions and causes implementation receives the prize. The result is a revised manual that becomes the new current manual.
2. **A strict improvement exists.** Then whoever builds and implements that improvement receives the prize instead, provided it dominates the Minimum Acceptable Governance function by function rather than skipping inconvenient pieces.

Those are the only serious possibilities. The unserious possibility is the one humans choose by default: endless argument with no implementation market. Either way, the prize converges on a better instruction manual and causes its implementation. People are dying at {{< var global_disease_deaths_daily_nounit >}} per day while your species argues about mechanism design. Please improve the manual as quickly as possible.

> Reward whoever causes the most people to stop dying and start earning more, using any legal method, or replace the current best attempt with a better one.

One institution may initiate the network. No institution should be able to stop it.

The mechanism does not need participants to be wise. It needs them to be self-interested, impatient, and capable of reading a scoreboard. The remaining variable is how long this takes to become obvious enough to act on.
